question: Which of the following is a variety of coffee beans, mainly produced in South India?
solution:
The correct answer is **Arabica. ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The two main varieties of coffee viz., Arabica and Robusta are grown in India. **
 
• Arabica is a mild coffee, but the beans being more aromatic, it has higher market value compared to Robusta beans.
 
• On the other hand, Robusta has more strength and is, therefore, used in making various blends.
 
• Arabica is grown in higher altitudes than Robusta. 
 
• The cool and equable temperature, ranging between 15°C to 25°C, is suitable for Arabica while for Robusta, a hot and humid climate with temperatures ranging from 20°C to 30°C is suitable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd14b80eaccaf97820b5e23c890fd2df350c6856a292338dfcc92d1810302c62.png] 

 
• Indian coffee has created a niche for itself in the international market and the Indian Coffees are earning a high premium, particularly Indian Robusta which is highly preferred for its good blending quality. 
 
• Arabica Coffee from India is also well received in the international market.
 
• Arabica is susceptible to pests & diseases such as White Stem Borer, leaf rust, etc., and requires more shade than Robusta. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The harvest of Arabica takes place between November to January, while for Robusta it is December to February.
 
• In India, coffee is traditionally grown in the Western Ghats spread over Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu. 
 
• Coffee cultivation is also being expanding rapidly in the nontraditional areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as well as in the North-East states.
 
• Brazil is, quite simply, the largest coffee producer in the world. 
 
• In 2016 it is thought that 2,595,000 metric tons of coffee beans were produced in Brazil alone.
